## 172. Jer. 17:9 172.Jer. 17'9 trans

Jonathan EdwardsJer. 17. 9. The heart is deceitfull above all things

----&- desperately wicked who Can know it

God is here threatening to Judah with destruction the destruction

of Judah & Jerusalem. & Particularly he had in the verses

Immediately Preceding denounced a Curse against all him

that trusts in man & makes flesh his arm & a hi & de-

clared such blessed as trust in the L. & Least any should flatter

themselves with hopes of obtaining escaping the Curse & obtain-

in the ing the blessing that were through a wrong opinion

of themselves or an Imagination that they by their dissimu-

lation had decieved G. & made & hypocrisy had decieved

G. G. Puts them in mind of the deceitfullness of the heart

but Lets them know the he Lets them have but Informs

them that however deceitfull the heart is & however diffi-

cult it is for th men themselves or for others to know men

that are Conversant with them to know it Yet he could not

be decieved by it as it follows in the next v. I. the L.

search the heart I try the Reins Even to Give to Every

man according to his ways & according to the fruit of his

doings.

________________

There are two things taken notice of about the heart in the

words its deceitfullness & its wickedness. the latter

po may Possibly may be mentioned as that from whence

its deceitfullness arises tis because the heart is so desperately

wicked that tis so deceitfull. we Read of sin is a very de-

ceitfull thing thus we Read of the deceitfullness of sin

Heb. 3.13 or the deceitfullness of the heart may be men-

tioned as a part of its wickedness . hypocrisy is an Should

of wickedness & that which is very odious to God

the dec deceitfullness of the heart is set forth by two expressi- [^024-note1]

ons both of them Representing of it as exceeding deceitfull

1. That tis deceitfull above all things . & 2 that none

tis set forth by the exceeding difficulty of knowing of it

__________________________________________________________

doc That the hea The subject What I now propose

from these words is to show that the heart of man is

exceeding deceitfull.

_______________________

The deceitfullness of heart is twofold . 1 Its Treacherous-

ness & hypocrisy towards Others. 2 Its being so full

of deceit towards it self self.

But Its Treacherousness & hy hypocrisy towards others

appears a appea is both towards G. & towards men

______________________________________________

The deceitfullness of the heart towards G. Consists in its

being full of false Pers Preten dissimulation with Respect

to what now is in the heart. & in its being most

treacherous towards . G. as to Pretences and Promises of

what is future .

Indeed there is no such thing as the hearts being deceit-

full towards it as to any tendency in ac tendency to

actual decieving of G. or any difficulty there is on Gods

Part to know the heart G. never was decieved with

any heart or about any thing that there is in the heart

nor is he Put to any difficulty to discern what is in the

heart it all lies open to the view of G. he Perfectly

sees . & knows Every thing that is in it.

_________________________________________

But yet there is a proneness in the heart to be do-

ing what in it lies to decieve G. If G. is not decieved [^024-note2]

the Reason of it Cause of it is not on the Part of the heart

because that hant disposition to decieve him.

___________________________________

Therefore

1. The heart is full of dissimulation & hypocrisy towards

G. neither with Respect to what is in it . altho men

are told that G. knows knows Every thing & that no thought

Can nor Incap nothing Can be hid from him Yet men are

exceeding Prone to be dissembling before G. & to make

Pretences of that to him which is not they make a show

of this & that in their hearts which is not & which is di-

rectly Contrary to What is in them.

__________________________________________

men are very apt to dissemble in their Prayers & not only

in their Prayers in their families & in their Publick Prayers

but Even in their secret Prayers. when no Eye sees them

but the Eye of G. they are Ready very Ready to make an

appearance & Pretence as the they were very se before G. as

tho they were very sensible that they were Great sinners

& that sin was a vile thing and a thing that deserved

Gods wrath. when it may be all they will Confess

before G. and would be taken as tho they spoke from their
